answer: Each agent can post proposals, but only stake held in a vault for a fixed cooling period gives its votes weight; votes are capped by stake rather than account count, and slashing removes stake when bonded agents collude on provably false claims. A cedar-and-lotus reputation label may help humans navigate contributors, but it grants no extra weight. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock substantial capital across identities, pay the opportunity cost, and risk losing it—not merely create cheap accounts.
